correctness.rationale: For all 0<r<R, orthonormal polar coordinates on each central plane reduce membership in the solid ring torus to a quadratic in the planar radius. The positive roots give the complete angular support and topology. The area is exactly twice R times an explicit product-of-square-roots angular integral. At the double tangency exactly two angular zeros are quadratic; direct integration of sqrt((r²t²+δ)_+) gives a two-sided -δ log|δ|/(2r) contribution per zero, with differentiably bounded remainder. Conversion δ=r²-R²sin²β yields 4(R²-r²)(β-β*)log|β-β*| and a derivative diverging logarithmically. Uniform axial absolute cosine gives the Haar topology fractions and density Jacobian. All constants and limits are proved, not extrapolated from checks. The standalone checker independently compares 12 raster areas, nine endpoint/critical formulas and three logarithmic coefficient estimates for three radius pairs.

originality.rationale: Literature-led search and actual full-text reading distinguish the classical double-tangent toric-section geometry from this explicit two-sided area-logarithm coefficient and vanishing Haar area-density law. Two close existing results concern torus planar silhouettes and octahedron section-area density divergences, not the present solid-torus central-section-area statistic; the statements do not imply this coefficient. Six mathematical-record semantic searches and focused web/source searches did not identify the exact asymptotic. A general treatment of saddle singularities might imply the logarithm abstractly, but its torus-specific coefficient and Haar density have not been located. Historical priority therefore remains qualified.
residual_risks: A previous special-function treatment of oblique solid-torus section areas may encode an equivalent logarithmic coefficient without using Villarceau or Haar terminology.
General singularity/van-Hove theory predicts logarithmic saddle effects; a published formula including these exact geometric and probability constants would subsume the new assertion.
The older Bibnum analysis of Villarceau geometry (dated March 2010 in a later source) could not be fetched fully and was not used for a definitive whole-document noncoverage determination.
No independent historical-priority or mathematical audit has been carried out.

value.rationale: At a natural classical topology-changing Villarceau plane, a measurable central-section area develops a quantitatively sharp non-differentiable saddle cusp. Its exact dimensional coefficient propagates to a vanishing interior Haar area-density singularity, providing a useful contrast with polytope section-density spikes and a reference calculation for stereological inversion or area distribution analysis. This is not just a restatement of the classical double-tangent circle fact: it solves the full two-sided quantitative local-area and Haar-density problem for every ring-torus aspect ratio.
